cd-cup-product.title: Singular cohomology and the cup product

questions.q: Cochains are defined by $C^n(X;\mathbb{Z}) = \Hom(C_n(X),\mathbb{Z})$ and the coboundary $\delta\colon C^n\to C^{n+1}$ is given by:
questions.explain: The coboundary is the transpose of $\partial$: evaluate the cochain on the boundary of an $(n{+}1)$-simplex. Then $\delta^2 = 0$ falls out of $\partial^2 = 0$.

questions.q: On $T^2 = S^1\times S^1$, the cohomology ring is $H^*(T^2;\mathbb{Z}) = \Lambda[\alpha,\beta]$ with $|\alpha|=|\beta|=1$. What is $\alpha\smile\alpha$?
questions.explain: The cup product is graded-commutative: $\alpha\smile\beta = (-1)^{|\alpha||\beta|}\beta\smile\alpha$. For an odd-degree class $\alpha$, this forces $\alpha\smile\alpha = -\alpha\smile\alpha$, i.e. $2(\alpha\smile\alpha) = 0$, and integrally $\alpha\smile\alpha = 0$ in the exterior algebra.
$H^*(T^2;\mathbb{Z})\cong\Lambda[\alpha,\beta]$ has one generator in each degree $0,2$ and two in degree $1$. So $\mathrm{rk}\,H^2 = 1$, generated by $\alpha\smile\beta$.

questions.q: For $X = U\cup V$ with $U,V$ open, the cohomology Mayer–Vietoris sequence reads $\cdots\to H^n(X)\to H^n(U)\oplus H^n(V)\to H^n(U\cap V)\xrightarrow{\delta} H^{n+1}(X)\to\cdots$. Which property is responsible for the connecting homomorphism $\delta$ raising degree?
choices: The short exact sequence of cochain complexes induces a long exact sequence going up in degree
The Eilenberg–Steenrod axioms forbid downward maps
questions.explain: Mayer–Vietoris comes from a short exact sequence of cochain complexes $0\to C^*(X)\to C^*(U)\oplus C^*(V)\to C^*(U\cap V)\to 0$. The standard zigzag of the snake lemma gives a long exact sequence; the connecting homomorphism shifts up in cohomology (down in homology).

questions.q: Künneth over a field $k$ states $H^*(X\times Y;k)\cong H^*(X;k)\otimes_k H^*(Y;k)$. What is the corresponding statement over $\mathbb{Z}$?
choices: Always an isomorphism, by the same proof
$H_n(X\times Y;\mathbb{Z}) \cong \bigoplus_{p+q=n} H_p(X)\otimes H_q(Y)$ with no correction
There is a short exact sequence $0\to\bigoplus H_p(X)\otimes H_q(Y)\to H_n(X\times Y)\to\bigoplus\mathrm{Tor}(H_p(X),H_q(Y))\to 0$
questions.explain: The integral Künneth formula has a Tor correction term: it is short-exact with $\bigoplus_{p+q=n-1}\mathrm{Tor}_1^{\mathbb{Z}}(H_p(X),H_q(Y))$ on the right. Over a field, Tor vanishes.
$H^*(\mathbb{CP}^n;\mathbb{Z})\cong\mathbb{Z}[x]/(x^{n+1})$ with $|x|=2$. So $H^{2k}$ is a free $\mathbb{Z}$-module of rank 1 for $0\le k\le n$, generated by $x^k$. For $n=3,k=2$ the rank is $1$.

questions.q: Poincaré duality for a closed oriented $n$-manifold $M$ says $H^k(M)\cong H_{n-k}(M)$. Which structure on $M$ is essential for the statement?
choices: An orientation, or equivalently a fundamental class $[M]\in H_n(M;\mathbb{Z})$
questions.explain: The duality is induced by capping with the fundamental class. Without orientation only $\mathbb{Z}/2$ coefficients work; without compactness one must use compactly supported cohomology on one side.

questions.q: Let $\Sigma_g$ be the closed orientable surface of genus $g$. Which of the following Betti numbers (over $\mathbb{Q}$) are correct? Select all that apply.
questions.explain: $\Sigma_g$ is connected and oriented, so $b_0=b_2=1$. The first homology has rank $2g$ (the $a$ and $b$ cycles); Poincaré duality $b_1=b_{2-1}=b_1$ is consistent. Choice $b_1=g$ is the dimension of the space of holomorphic 1-forms (Hodge $h^{1,0}$), not the Betti number.

questions.q: For $\mathbb{CP}^n$, Poincaré duality $H^k(\mathbb{CP}^n)\cong H_{2n-k}(\mathbb{CP}^n)$ holds for which dimensions $k$? Enter the value of $k$ such that $H^k=H_k=\mathbb{Z}$ when $n=4$ and $k$ is the largest such integer with $k=2n-k$.
questions.explain: The fixed point of $k\mapsto 2n-k$ is $k=n$. For $\mathbb{CP}^4$ ($n=4$, real dimension $8$), this is $k=4$, and indeed $H^4(\mathbb{CP}^4)=H_4(\mathbb{CP}^4)=\mathbb{Z}$.

cd-de-rham.title: De Rham cohomology and the de Rham theorem

questions.q: The de Rham theorem identifies $H^*_{\mathrm{dR}}(M;\mathbb{R})$ with $H^*(M;\mathbb{R})$ via:
choices: Pulling back along the identity map
questions.explain: The de Rham pairing $\Omega^k(M)\times C_k(M)\to\mathbb{R}$, $(\omega,\sigma)\mapsto\int_\sigma\omega$, descends to a perfect pairing of cohomology with real homology by Stokes's theorem. The induced map $H^k_{\mathrm{dR}}\to H^k(M;\mathbb{R})$ is an isomorphism.

questions.q: Under the de Rham isomorphism, the cup product on singular cohomology corresponds to which operation on forms?
questions.explain: The wedge product of closed forms is closed and descends to a graded-commutative product on $H^*_{\mathrm{dR}}$ matching cup product on the singular side. This compatibility is part of de Rham's theorem (often called the de Rham–Whitney isomorphism of rings).
$T^2 = S^1\times S^1$ has $b_1 = 2$ (one cycle for each factor), and $H^1_{\mathrm{dR}}(T^2)$ is generated by the closed-but-not-exact $1$-forms $d\theta_1, d\theta_2$.

questions.q: On the $r$-th page of a cohomological spectral sequence, the differential $d_r$ has bidegree:
questions.explain: Differentials on $E_r^{p,q}$ shift filtration degree by $r$ and total degree by $1$, hence raise $p$ by $r$ and change $q$ by $1-r$. So $d_r\colon E_r^{p,q}\to E_r^{p+r,q-r+1}$.

questions.q: For the Serre spectral sequence of the Hopf fibration $S^1\hookrightarrow S^3\to S^2$, the $E_2$ page is $E_2^{p,q} = H^p(S^2;H^q(S^1;\mathbb{Z}))$. Where does the only non-zero differential $d_2$ originate?
questions.explain: The only non-zero entries are at $(0,0),(0,1),(2,0),(2,1)$ each $=\mathbb{Z}$. The differential $d_2\colon E_2^{0,1}\to E_2^{2,0}$ sends the generator of $H^1(S^1)$ to the Euler class of the Hopf bundle, which is a generator of $H^2(S^2)$. This $d_2$ is an isomorphism, killing both $E_2^{0,1}$ and $E_2^{2,0}$ — leaving only $H^0(S^3)$ and $H^3(S^3)$ on $E_\infty$.

questions.q: For the Serre spectral sequence of $S^1\hookrightarrow S^3\to S^2$, what is the rank of $E_\infty^{2,1}$? (This is what survives all differentials in bidegree $(2,1)$.)
questions.explain: $E_2^{2,1}=H^2(S^2)\otimes H^1(S^1)=\mathbb{Z}$. No differential lands in or leaves $(2,1)$ on $E_2$ (the differentials kill $(0,1)$ and $(2,0)$ instead), so $E_\infty^{2,1}=\mathbb{Z}$, contributing to $H^3(S^3)=\mathbb{Z}$.

questions.q: Stiefel–Whitney classes $w_i(\xi)$ of a real vector bundle $\xi\to B$ live in which cohomology group?
questions.explain: Stiefel–Whitney classes are mod 2 invariants: $w_i\in H^i(B;\mathbb{Z}/2)$. Working mod 2 lets one ignore orientation issues — every real bundle has $w_i$, but only oriented ones have an Euler class in integer cohomology.

questions.q: The total Chern class satisfies the Whitney sum formula:
questions.explain: The total Chern class $c(\xi)=1+c_1+c_2+\cdots$ is multiplicative under direct sum: $c(\xi\oplus\eta)=c(\xi)\smile c(\eta)$. This is one of the few honest non-trivial uses of the cup product in introductory characteristic class theory.

questions.q: Let $\gamma$ be the tautological line bundle on $\mathbb{CP}^n$. Then $c_1(\gamma)$ generates $H^2(\mathbb{CP}^n;\mathbb{Z})$. What is $c_1(\gamma)^n$ as an element of $H^{2n}(\mathbb{CP}^n;\mathbb{Z})\cong\mathbb{Z}$, expressed as the integer coefficient on the generator (up to sign)?
questions.explain: $H^*(\mathbb{CP}^n;\mathbb{Z})=\mathbb{Z}[x]/(x^{n+1})$ with $x = -c_1(\gamma)$ (Milnor–Stasheff sign convention) or $x=c_1(\gamma)$ depending on author. Either way $c_1(\gamma)^n$ is the generator of $H^{2n}$, so the integer coefficient is $\pm 1$.
